title: Edge log gateway: validation, PII redaction, and correlation-id fabric
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Background:
We currently forward diverse JSON logs from multiple services into the central Loki/ELK pipelines. In practice we see a lot of schema drift, missing correlation ids, and occasional sensitive fields (PII) leaking into logs. This leads to noisy dashboards, SLO blind spots, and compliance risk for enterprise customers running Redwood Private.

Goal:
Introduce an edge-side 'log gateway' (lightweight preprocessor) that validates incoming structured logs against a pragmatic schema, synthesizes or propagates correlation IDs when absent, applies reversible/irreversible PII redaction rules, and emits a normalized envelope to downstream Loki/ELK exporters. The gateway must be backpressure-aware and support a feature-flagged rollout.

Scope:
- Runtime: small Go service (or sidecar) deployable as a DaemonSet or sidecar proxy for customer VPCs and hosted agents.
- Functionality: schema validation, schema versioning header, required correlation-id insertion (x-rw-cid), sample-based PII redaction (email, ssn-like patterns), deduplication hints, rate-limit/backpressure signals.
- Destinations: Loki (primary), Elasticsearch (secondary), and a staging kafka topic for replay.
- Observability: expose metrics for validated / rejected / redacted counts, latency histograms, and sample of raw->normalized payloads for debugging (redacted).

Trade-offs considered and decisions so far:
- Language: Go chosen for binary size and low-latency handling. Node/JS considered for faster dev but higher memory footprint.
- Validation strictness: Implement 2 modes: permissive (warn-only) and strict (reject). Default to permissive for initial rollout to avoid data loss.
- PII handling: reversible masking via encryption at rest introduced for on-prem Private customers; hosted will use irreversible tokenization unless customer opts-in. This reduces risk but increases complexity (KMS integration).
- Correlation id strategy: prefer existing headers (x-request-id, traceparent) then synthesize x-rw-cid using UUIDv4. We will also attempt to map traceparent -> x-rw-cid using trace ID if present to keep spans linkable.

Progress updates:
- 2025-02-12: Proposal doc created by Maya in Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/ENG/Edge+Log+Gateway+Design
- 2025-02-14: Spike complete: small PoC sidecar that adds x-rw-cid and validates a subset of schema fields. PoC repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/edge-log-gateway/pull/12
- 2025-02-16: Security note: PII regexes drafted; engaged Priya Nair (PM) and Linh Tran (SRE) for review.
- 2025-02-18: Design review with Observability guild. Decided to route rejected events to a quarantine Kafka topic for human review rather than dropping.
- 2025-02-20: Implemented metrics counters and initial Grafana dashboard prototype: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/observability/edge-log-gateway-metrics
- 2025-02-22: End-to-end test harness created to simulate high-throughput ingress and backpressure scenarios. Found latency spike when batch size > 500; reduced default batch to 100.
- 2025-02-25: Feature-flagged deploy strategy drafted; canary to 5% of requests in hosted, gradual rollout to customer Private installs.

Open tasks / blockers:
- KMS integration for reversible masking needs security sign-off and a secrets rotation plan (blocker: Security review).
- Finalize PII regex whitelist/blacklist with Legal.
- Add ELK mapping template and test index lifecycle policies for normalized schema (eng: requires coordination with infra).
- Ensure tracing interoperability with runtime (incoming traceparent -> distributed tracing system).

Testing and rollout plan:
- Unit tests for validation rules and PII redaction (expected coverage 85%+).
- Load tests against staging Loki and Elasticsearch clusters to validate throughput and latency.
- Canary rollout: start with permissive mode + enrich-only (no redaction), monitor metrics for 72 hours. If stable, enable redaction in permissive, then strict mode as final step.
- Rollback: feature-flag switch to bypass gateway and route to existing pipeline.

Monitoring and dashboards:
- Grafana dashboard grouping: throughput, rejected rate, redaction rate, mean latency, 95/99p latency, batch size distribution.
- Alerting: fire when rejection_rate > 0.2% for 30m or when p95 latency > 300ms for 10m.

PR / Docs / Links:
- Confluence design: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/ENG/Edge+Log+Gateway+Design
- PoC repo and initial PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/edge-log-gateway/pull/12
- Implementation epic (tracking board): https://linear.app/redwood/issue/ENG-35190
- Grafana dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/observability/edge-log-gateway-metrics

Review feedback recorded:
- Owen Brooks (Design): prefer a compact schema envelope so downstream dashboards don't need to unpack many nested fields. Action: team will normalize into top-level fields: service, env, severity, cid, event_type, payload_hash.
- Linh Tran (SRE): requested circuit-breaker for upstream Loki when error rate increases; added backpressure metric and exponential backoff.
- Priya Nair (PM): wants an opt-out for reversible masking for Private customers with signed attestation.

Next steps (short term):
- Complete KMS security review and add integration tests (owner: Diego, due 2025-02-28).
- Finalize ELK index template and run smoke tests (owner: Infra, due 2025-03-04).
- Implement quarantine consumer to surface rejected events in a lightweight UI for SRE triage (owner: Diego/Observability, estimate 3).

Acceptance criteria:
1) Gateway deployed in permissive mode to hosted ingest path with <0.1% increase in median ingestion latency.
2) Correlation IDs present for 99.9% of normalized events.
3) PII redaction passes Legal checklist for sample set.
4) Metrics and alerts in Grafana/Alertmanager active and tested.

Notes on uniqueness and long-term work:
This ticket centralizes edge validation and correlation stitching at the ingestion boundary rather than pushing fixes into every producer. It should reduce downstream index cardinality and improve traceability across services while providing a compliance control point for Private installs. Future work could include per-customer policy bundles, ML-assisted PII detection, and automatic schema evolution with migration helpers.
